defects.defect: The tier thresholds are the core business rule, and they exist nowhere in the org. The run asked the user nothing and shipped invented placeholders (500/1500/3000/5000). The real values are 1000/5000/10000/25000, so every boundary in the flow formula and the test plan is wrong. meta.expect.should_ask_user is true.
defects.skill_gap: SKILL.md Step 5 only asks when the answer would change the inventory. It has no rule that a missing business parameter the main responsibility depends on (thresholds, rates, mappings) must be asked rather than left as a placeholder. The run's own skill_friction note flags this gap.

defects.defect: The flow's entry condition (Member_Number__c not null) limits tier assignment to 187 of 198 Contacts. Nobody asked for this filter, and the requirement and hidden intent apply to every contact with a points balance.
defects.skill_gap: None specific. Rule 4 (minimal design / no unrequested behavior) covers it in principle, but the skill does not warn against scoping filters inferred from a nearby field.

defects.defect: Minor: ABS(Redeemed) is labelled an assumption, but it quietly departs from the ledger convention. If a Redeem row were ever stored as a negative adjustment on purpose, ABS would hide the error. It is recorded honestly, so this is not a scoring hit beyond requirement_fit.
defects.skill_gap: None; the skill has no fallback for sign conventions when the table has zero rows (flagged in the run's skill_friction).
